audit_result.proof_trace: The consent server action reads `redirect_uri` from formData (line 19) and uses it directly to store in the auth code DB record and to redirect — with no validation against `application.redirect_uris`. The only redirect_uri guard is in `GET /oauth/authorize` (route.ts:94), but the consent page (`/oauth/authorize/consent`) is directly accessible with no routing guard, allowing an attacker to bypass the authorize endpoint entirely and supply an arbitrary `redirect_uri` via query parameters. The token endpoint's check (token/route.ts:90) compares the submitted URI against the stored auth code value, which is the already-tampered URI, so it does not detect the bypass.
audit_result.attack_scenario: Attacker crafts a direct URL to `/oauth/authorize/consent?client_id=VALID_CLIENT&redirect_uri=https://evil.com/steal&state=x&code_challenge=ATTACKER_HASH&code_challenge_method=S256&app_name=LegitApp`, social-engineers a logged-in victim to visit and approve; auth code is issued to `https://evil.com/steal`, attacker exchanges it for an access token using the PKCE verifier they control.

PROP-oauth-2-0-ut-pre-005.text: redirect_uri must match a pre-registered URI for the resolved client application.
PROP-oauth-2-0-ut-pre-005.assertion: isValidRedirectUri(redirectUri, application.redirect_uris) == true before auth code grant
